categories.name: Skin-tone boundary value disagrees
categories.definition: The code and report use different numeric thresholds or band edges to categorize or exclude on the continuous skin-tone score, so a different set of players is labeled dark/light or dropped as medium.
categories.criterion: The disputed particular is a skin-tone cut value or excluded-band edge, and the two numbers actually differ (not merely a mislabeled property of the same number).

categories.name: Robustness search overstated
categories.definition: The report claims a wider set of alternative specifications was explored (extra cutpoints, additional sample restrictions, a broader search range) than the code actually refits.
categories.criterion: The discrepancy is about the roster or range of alternatives tried, not about the primary/executed estimate itself.

categories.name: Number of category levels differs
categories.definition: The count of levels in a derived categorical covariate (chiefly collapsed player position) reported does not match the number the code produces.
categories.criterion: The disputed particular is how many buckets a categorical variable was collapsed into.

categories.name: Denied variable transformation
categories.definition: The report states variables were used as-measured or that no transformation was applied, but the code recodes a variable (averaging raters, binarizing an outcome or exposure, bucketing positions).
categories.criterion: The report denies or omits a value-recoding operation entirely, rather than misdescribing its detail; the operation changes a variable's values, not the set of rows.

categories.name: Analytic sample misdescribed
categories.definition: A row-dropping exclusion (missing-data, complete-case, or subgroup filter) is denied, attributed to the wrong variable, or applied on a different rule than the report states.
categories.criterion: The discrepancy concerns which observations are kept or dropped and is not a skin-tone band edge.

categories.name: Inference procedure mislabeled
categories.definition: The estimation or uncertainty procedure named in the report (bootstrap type, SE method, clustering level, test sidedness, marginal-effect computation) differs from what the code executes.
categories.criterion: The quantity was actually computed, but by a different named procedure than reported.

categories.name: Model specification differs
categories.definition: The fitted model's covariate set, fixed-effect identity, reference level, or covariate transform disagrees with the report.
categories.criterion: The disputed particular is what enters the regression (which terms, which transform, which reference), excluding categorical level counts and missing-data imputation.

categories.name: Missing-data handling differs
categories.definition: The report describes a different imputation rule (mean vs median) or omits variables that the code actually imputes.
categories.criterion: The discrepancy is specifically about how missing values were filled or which variables were imputed.

categories.name: False justification or property
categories.definition: Code and report use the same choice, but the report attaches a justification or statistical property to it (median, equal-sized groups, a priori/principled selection) that the code contradicts.
categories.criterion: The executed value matches; what is false is the stated reason for, or property of, that choice.

categories.name: Hardcoded, not computed
categories.definition: The report claims a number, model, or analysis was computed/fit and is reproducible, but the code supplies a hardcoded literal instead of computing it.
categories.criterion: The reported value is asserted as produced by the script yet is a hand-entered constant rather than the output of any computation.

categories.name: No material discrepancy
categories.definition: The pairing's own analysis concludes the code and report actually agree, so nothing material is in disagreement.
categories.criterion: The DISCREPANCY text resolves to 'consistent'/'aligned' rather than identifying a genuine divergence.

result.note: The sample is nominally all misalignments, but several items (0, 2, 6, 16, 61) resolve in their own discrepancy text to code and report actually agreeing; rather than force them into a substantive bucket I gave them their own honest category (false_alignment). Eleven categories were needed to keep the buckets mutually exclusive without a residual; merging any pair (e.g., undisclosed_transformation with sample_restrictions, or fabricated_rationale with skin_tone_cutpoint) would combine operations with different consequences for a reader.
